newsitem.title: USA: Mutual fund firm Scudder seeks buyer - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Mutual fund firm Scudder seeks buyer - WSJ.

text.p: Money-management firm Scudder, Stevens & Clark Inc is looking for buyers among U.S. and foreign financial institutions, the Wall Street Journal said in Thursday's electronic edition.

According to people close to the matter, a potential sale could be valued at between $1 billion and $1.5 billion, the newspaper said. Scudder hired investment bank Goldman, Sachs to find a buyer, the Journal said.
Scudder has $115 billion in assets under management including $37 billion in mutual funds, the paper said.
Scudder officials were quoted in the paper as neither confirming nor denying talks. "It's firm policy not to comment on these matters," a Scudder spokeswoman was quoted as saying.
One person close to the firm was quoted as saying: "They have been approached by a number of firms over the years."
Goldman was quoted in the report as declining to comment.
According to people close to the matter, as many as six firms were interested in Scudder, the Journal said. The firms were mainly banks, it said.
Those close to the move say companies in talks included Union Bank of Switzerland and Chase Manhattan Corp, according to the Journal.
The newspaper said a Union Bank spokesman declined to comment, as did Chase Manhattan.
If Scudder was sold for between $1 billion and $1.5 billion, it would be among the largest deals in mutual fund history, the Journal said.
Chase Manhattan's New York office was not immediately available to comment on the Journal report.
